protocol.epistemicBoundary: Model names are not treated as unitary theories. A conflict is admitted only for the strongest explicit claim under the stated target/scope; empirical support for one mechanism does not prove universal exclusivity.

models.name: Symbolic Action Pipeline
models.scope: discrete and semantic Game actions, including indirect control
models.coreClaim: participant intent/input must be mapped to candidate GameAction/control and resolved under current Game authority before consequence

models.name: Internal/Predictive Model Control
models.scope: sensorimotor tasks where prediction of body/environment dynamics is behaviorally relevant
models.coreClaim: learned predictive representations/state estimates contribute to control and adaptation

models.name: Optimal Feedback / Minimum Intervention
models.scope: goal-directed motor control with task-relevant costs and redundant degrees of freedom
models.coreClaim: control selectively corrects deviations that threaten task goals and can tolerate variability in task-irrelevant dimensions

models.name: Ecological Affordance / Direct Perception
models.primaryTarget: actor-environment possibility and information for action
models.scope: embodied action where actor/environment scaling and information specify possibilities
models.coreClaim: action possibilities depend on actor-environment relations and can regulate action through information without reducing the explanandum to symbolic rule descriptions
notClaimed: all symbolic actions are ecological affordances

models.name: Constraints-led / Dynamical Coordination
models.scope: perception-action systems under interacting actor/task/environment constraints
models.coreClaim: coordination solutions emerge under interacting constraints and can vary structurally while preserving function
notClaimed: no internal state can ever matter
all Game rules are physical constraints

models.name: Motor Program / Schema
models.scope: especially discrete or parameterized movement families and transfer
models.coreClaim: generalized action organization and parameterization can support production/generalization of learned movement classes
notClaimed: all skilled movement is fully precomputed/open-loop

models.name: Speed-Accuracy / Information-Theoretic
models.scope: tasks with spatial target tolerance/distance and movement-time pressure
models.coreClaim: movement time and accuracy constraints vary systematically with task difficulty in the specified task family

models.name: Sense-of-Agency Comparator/Inference
models.scope: human intentional action and judged agency
models.coreClaim: agency judgments can integrate action-feedback correspondence with goal/performance/contextual inference

models.name: Shared / Assistive / Hierarchical Control
models.coreClaim: different controllers can own different variables/layers/time intervals; raw command share is insufficient to characterize control

models.name: Skill as Conditional Capability Profile
models.primaryTarget: learned capability underlying performance across conditions
models.scope: specified task family and relevant condition/probe space
models.coreClaim: skill should be inferred from a learned, history-dependent conditional performance profile rather than identified with one observed score

conflicts.reason: Game semantic admission/action identity and Human sensorimotor implementation are different targets. A predictive controller can sit inside the expression/execution side of a symbolic GameAction contract.

Strong versions conflict over whether internally represented predictive dynamics are necessary for online action versus sufficiently informative organism-environment coupling. The admitted evidence establishes actor-relative affordances and predictive adaptation separately but does not justify a universal exclusivity verdict.
Prediction/state estimation can be part of an optimal-feedback controller; M2 emphasizes learned predictive representation while M3 emphasizes task-dependent correction policy/cost structure.

conflicts.discriminatingPrediction: If skilled control universally reproduces one desired trajectory, successful trials should minimize variability across all movement dimensions; if task-relevant stabilization/minimum intervention holds, redundant dimensions may remain variable while task goals stay stable.

conflicts.reason: A strong pre-specified fixed-program account conflicts with context-sensitive emergent/adaptive coordination; weaker schema/program accounts can coexist with online constraint-dependent parameterization and feedback.

conflicts.discriminatingPrediction: If skilled execution is fully precomputed after initiation, online state/error changes should not support systematic within-action correction; feedback/predictive control accounts expect condition-dependent correction when time/information permit.

conflicts.reason: Fitts-style speed-accuracy models provide useful task-family performance laws but cannot identify Skill across transfer, retention, timing, strategy, remapping or perturbation.

conflicts.discriminatingPrediction: If subjective agency is monotonic in exact command execution, computer assistance that suppresses commands must reduce agency; Wen et al. observed improved agency ratings under assistance in delayed/uncertain conditions despite many commands not executing.

If manual execution is universally superior control, assistance that suppresses erroneous low-level commands cannot improve both task performance and experienced control under the same high-level goal.

If current practice score is Skill, groups/conditions with better acquisition performance should necessarily show at least as good delayed retention/transfer; contextual-interference and guidance experiments can reverse that ordering.

If globally lower movement variability is always skill, variability should fall across all degrees/dimensions. Optimal-feedback/UCM accounts instead predict task-dependent variability structure; Auto Orbit shows lower timing/action-sequence variability can be skill-relevant in that particular task.

If ecological affordance and GameAction availability are identical, formal rule changes or symbolic commands should not change legal Game actions without corresponding actor-environment physical possibility change; games routinely permit/prohibit semantic actions by rule authority while physical possibility remains unchanged.

skillReconstruction.from: SkillState as one latent learned condition-relative capability
skillReconstruction.to: SkillProfile as a learned, history-dependent conditional capability surface over a declared task family and probe/condition space
skillReconstruction.formalSketch: P(task-relevant performance variables | participant/agent history, task family, current condition, mapping, perturbation)
guards: SkillProfile is not one universal scalar
probe dimensions are evidence windows, not mandatory components of every Skill
peak performance and robustness are not globally ordered
lower variability matters only relative to task-relevant variables
learning requires durable/history-dependent capability change, not transient performance improvement
